 ר' מנחם איש גליא \- [Tosefta\_Eruvin\_(Lieberman).8.9](sefaria:Tosefta_Eruvin_\(Lieberman\).8.9) \- " ר' מנחם איש גליא אומ' צנור שעלו בו קוצים וקישושות"  
The Talmud is citing the Tosefta. As mentioned earlier, נחום \= מנחם. Jastrow, “[גליא](sefaria:Jastrow,_גַּלְיָא_I.1)”, assumes (reasonably) that he was from Gallia or Galatia in Asia Minor, and not from Gaul. Gaul is mentioned elsewhere in the Talmud ([Yevamot.63a.6](sefaria:Yevamot.63a.6)) as a far-away place. It’s also mentioned in [Rosh\_Hashanah.26a.18](sefaria:Rosh_Hashanah.26a.18), as a place that Rabbi Akiva traveled to.
